children: Fennec Pharmaceuticals announced Phase 2 STS-J01 results showing PEDMARK met its primary endpoint, significantly reducing cisplatin‑related hearing loss in pediatric and AYA patients in Japan.
Primary endpoint met: ASHA-defined hearing loss in 24.0% (6/25) vs 56.4% benchmark (P=0.001), demonstrating significant protection.
By Brock criteria 84% had Grade 0 hearing loss; no Grade 3 or Grade 4 hearing loss observed, indicating favorable audiologic outcomes.
Objective tumor responses in 23 of 24 evaluable patients (95.8%), showing no evidence of interference with cisplatin antitumor activity.
Prospective pharmacokinetics support the six‑hour PEDMARK administration interval as a mechanistic rationale for protection without compromising efficacy.
Fennec is pursuing registration in Japan and exploring partnering/licensing opportunities for PEDMARK.
